doc_name: Chairman of the Senate of Pakistan
text: The chairman of the Senate of Pakistan, known as the president-chair of the Senate, is a presiding official elected by the Senate members and serves a three-year term, as stipulated in Article 60(1)–60(2) of Part III, Chapter 2 of the Constitution of Pakistan. The Senate must elect a chairman and deputy chairman at its first meeting and whenever the office becomes vacant, with the term beginning on the day the member assumes office. During the president's absence, the chairman of the Senate performs presidential duties; if the chairman is also unavailable, the speaker of the National Assembly assumes these duties. The chairman is the first in the line of succession to the presidency, preceding the speaker of the National Assembly. The first chairman of the Senate was Retired Senior Justice Habibullah Khan Marwat, who served until 1977, and Wasim Sajjad holds the record for the longest tenure. Senator Yusuf Raza Gilani, elected to the Senate in the April 2024 election, became the current chairman, assuming office on 9 April 2024. The Senate was established to provide equal representation to all federating units, balancing provincial disparities in the National Assembly and promoting national cohesion and harmony. It serves as a legislative body representing provinces and territories, fostering equality, peace, and mutual understanding essential for national growth. After Pakistan's creation on 14 August 1947, the first Constituent Assembly, elected in December 1945, passed the Objectives Resolution on 12 March 1949, which later became part of the constitution. It was dissolved in 1954, and the Second Constituent Assembly, convened by the governor-general in 1955, passed the first constitution on 29 February 1956, which was promulgated on 23 March 1956 and provided for a unicameral legislature. From 14 August 1947 to 1 March 1956, the Government of India Act, 1935, remained in effect. On 7 October 1958, martial law was declared and the constitution was abrogated. A Constitution Commission was appointed in February 1960 to draft the 1962 Constitution, which introduced a presidential system with a unicameral legislature and was abrogated on 25 March 1969. A civil government, following the 1970 elections in December 1971, introduced an interim constitution in 1972. The comprehensive 1973 Constitution, finalized on 12 April and promulgated on 14 August 1973, established a parliamentary system with a bicameral legislature consisting of the National Assembly and the Senate. The Senate initially had 45 members, increased to 63 in 1977, 87 in 1985, and reached 100 in 2002 through a legal framework enacted on 21 August 2002; currently, there are 104 members. The Parliament of Pakistan comprises the president and the two legislative houses: the National Assembly and the Senate. The president is elected by members of both Houses of Parliament and the four provincial assemblies and may be removed or impeached by a resolution passed by not less than two-thirds of the total membership of Parliament in a joint sitting. If the president's office becomes vacant or if the president is absent or unable to perform duties, the chairman of the Senate, or if unavailable, the speaker of the National Assembly, acts as president until a new president is elected. The Parliament includes political parties such as the Independent, Muslim League (N), Muslim League (Q), Pakistan Peoples Party, and Balochistan Awami Party.
